blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights HCloud, a system for resource-efficient provisioning in shared cloud systems that balances performance and cost. The paper demonstrates that a hybrid approach combining reserved instances with on-demand provisioning, alongside a smart placement policy, can improve performance by 2.1x compared to using only on-demand instances and reduce costs by 46% compared to fully-reserved systems. A key insight is the importance of understanding application sensitivity to interference (noisy neighbors) and leveraging large instances to minimize external interference. The authors also introduce Quasar, a cluster manager that profiles jobs to estimate resource preferences and interference sensitivity, enabling better placement decisions. The study evaluates different provisioning strategies across static, low-variability, and high-variability workloads, showing that hybrid strategies outperform pure reserved or on-demand approaches in both performance and cost efficiency.
paper_title: HCloud: Resource-efficient provisioning in shared cloud systems
